html:
The Barada are an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, a little inland from the coast west of Mackay. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their speech was one of the varieties once grouped with the Biri language, though recent work suggests it was distinct. Little else is recorded. Neighbours on the map include the Koinmerburra on the coast, the Yuwi and the Barna. Pastoral runs and later sugar cane took over the Mackay district from the 1860s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
